sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Montpellier has combined two opposite policies: free public transport for residents and a steady widening of paid street parking. On 21 December 2023 the metropolis made public transport free every day for all its residents, who must first obtain a free pass [3]; ridership in the first quarter of 2024 was reported 23.7% above the first quarter of 2019, a comparison the article qualifies because the counting method changed [4]. Paid parking was extended to the Clémenceau-Rondelet sector in 2023, with checks due from 31 March 2023 and free 30-minute spaces created [0], and to the Ovalie-Grisettes sector from 15 September 2023, according to a city sheet [1]. As of the June 2023 sheet, a resident permit cost 15 euros a month or 150 euros a year, and 3 or 30 euros with a transit subscription [2].

Access to the old centre is being closed to cars. A February 2025 city leaflet planned to extend the pedestrian area south of the Comédie square, with access-control equipment installed since January and commissioning planned for summer 2025, and to turn the former Arceaux car park into a planted esplanade [10]. On the city's pedestrian-area page, parking is prohibited in the pedestrian areas, residents without a garage get 2 x 30 minutes a day and motor vehicles face fines of up to 135 euros [12]. On the low-emission zone, Connexion France reported on 5 February 2025 that 31 mayors had agreed to suspend fines until 2027, with the council vote still pending; the report is dated and may have been superseded [9].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The park-and-ride network is the main development. In March 2024 the nine P+tram car parks were open 24/7 for up to 24 hours, free for holders of the free pass who declare their transit trip, or at a package of 5.20 euros [5]; a leaflet from 2023 had announced a rise to 8 euros for others, which the March 2024 brochure does not confirm [6]. Tram line 5 opened on 20 December 2025, running about 16 km from Clapiers to Grés de Montpellier with 27 stops [15]. A pre-opening press kit says two new park-and-ride sites would bring the network to eleven, but it names the sites in different ways in different places, so we do not give their locations or capacities [14].

In the centre, a 2022 project letter planned to modernise the Comédie car park, with an entrance moved to avenue Frédéric Mistral, bike parking and charging zones, and works to finish in mid-2025 [13]. The metropolis had installed 66 charging stations with 150 charge points by January 2024 and planned 600 more public charge points with the operator E-totem [16].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
According to the city's parking page, seven city-centre car parks are managed by TaM (Antigone, Comédie, Corum, Europa, Gambetta, Saint-Roch and Hôtel de Ville), eight car parks in Montpellier and the surrounding area by the private Effia network and two by Indigo (Triangle and Peyrou-Pitot); the Polygone shopping centre has its own car park, and 16 car parks along the tram lines offer over 5,000 spaces, free for TaM subscribers [8]. The March 2024 brochure counts 12 car parks and 22,000 spaces in the centre, with capacities from 239 at Antigone to 1,973 at Polygone [7]. The metropolis publishes a location dataset of its multi-storey car parks on data.gouv.fr, with no live counts [17].

Our data cover 15 car parks with 8,628 spaces from the metropolis's live feed, measured since 5 October 2026. Occupancy averaged about 52% on weekdays and 43% at weekends, weighted by spaces, so the garages are in steady use. The fullest are Triangle (594 spaces, Indigo), which averaged 75%, Pitot (771) at 73%, Arc de Triomphe (451) at 72%, Euromédecine (350) at 72% and Saint-Roch (805) at 65%, with peaks of 88% to 94%; none was full for more than about 7% of the hours. The weekend drop is large at Saint-Roch (71% on weekdays, 50% at weekends) and at Occitanie (30% against 11%), and absent at Pitot and Triangle. The mayor said in April 2025 that city statistics show plenty of free spaces in Corum, Comédie, Pitot and Europa [11]; our readings show Europa at 33% and Corum at 45%, but Comédie at 59% and Pitot at 73%, so the statement fits some of these four more than others. The big outlier is Circé Odysseum (1,200 spaces), which averaged 17%, and Garcia Lorca (400) at 13%. These are two weeks of data.
